description:
This application seeks permission for a 4.72m rear extension designed to future proof the home by providing a ground floor shower room, allowing for the potential conversion of the front living room into a bedroom to accommodate changing lifestyle needs in the future, particularly for an elderly couple. In addition, the extension will provide a more spacious and functional open plan lounge and dining area, a slightly larger kitchen, and a more practical pantry, closet and utility room. The existing utility room offers limited space, making tasks such as bending to access the washing machine challenging. The proposed design takes mobility and accessibility into account by increasing the circulation space in this area.
A new side elevation window (WG02) is proposed, which will match the style of the existing windows. The client also wishes to replace the front facing windows, which have become inefficient due to condensation issues. The new white uPVC windows will retain the existing style but omit the crisscross glazing pattern to enhance natural light and provide an unobstructed view. New two rooflights has been proposed over the dining area to enhance light penetration into the proposed lounge. Great care has been taken to ensure the external appearance remains in keeping with the character of the existing property by matching materials, windows, and doors accordingly.
